caption: Traffic light sequence
colour: black box with red, amber and green lamps stacked vertically
explanation: Traffic lights always follow the order red, then red and amber together, then green, then amber, then back to red; red means stop and red and amber means stop (do not go until green shows), while amber means stop unless you are so close that stopping would be unsafe.
mnemonic: Red-and-amber is still STOP: get ready, but don't go.
notes: Composite traffic-light signal drawn in-app; no single official TSRGD SVG. Sequence per Highway Code rules 175-178.

caption: Green filter arrow
colour: black box with a green arrow lamp lit beside the main lights
explanation: A green filter arrow lit at traffic lights means you may move only in the direction the arrow points, whatever the other lights show; do not enter that lane unless you intend to go that way.
mnemonic: Green arrow = go that way only.
notes: Composite traffic-light signal drawn in-app; no single official TSRGD SVG. Highway Code rule 177.

caption: Flashing red stop lights
colour: two red lamps side by side flashing alternately
explanation: Twin flashing red lights mean you must stop, for example at level crossings, lifting bridges, airfields, fire and ambulance stations; do not cross or pass until the lights stop flashing.
mnemonic: Reds flashing = full stop, wait until they're off.
notes: Composite signal drawn in-app; no single official TSRGD SVG. Highway Code rule 293 (level crossings) and rules 175/270.

caption: Lane control signal
colour: overhead gantry sign: green down-arrow for open lane, red X for closed lane
explanation: Overhead lane signals control which lanes you may use: a green downward arrow means the lane is open, a red X means the lane is closed and you must move out of it, and a white diagonal arrow tells you to move to the lane it points to.
mnemonic: Green down = go, red X = get out of that lane.
notes: Composite overhead lane-control signal drawn in-app; no single official TSRGD SVG. Highway Code rules 255-258.
